cards.title: Introduction to Vue Events
cards.content:
In Vue.js, handling events is done using the v-on directive or its shorthand symbol, @.

You can listen to DOM events and run JavaScript upon triggering.

<button @click="count++">Add 1</button>

cards.title: Method Event Handlers
cards.content:
For more complex logic, you can bind an event to a method defined in your component's methods option or Composition API.

<button @click="greet">Greet</button>

The method will automatically receive the native DOM event as an argument if called directly.

cards.title: Fill in the Event Directive
cards.content: To listen to a submit event on a form while preventing its default reload, you use _____ prevent.

cards.title: Event Modifiers
cards.content:
Vue provides event modifiers for v-on so you don't have to call event.preventDefault() or event.stopPropagation() inside your methods.

  • .stop - call event.stopPropagation()
  • .prevent - call event.preventDefault()
  • .once - the event handler will be triggered at most once
<form @submit.prevent="onSubmit">...</form>

pairs.right: Triggers only if event.target is the element itself

cards.title: Key Modifiers and System Modifiers
cards.content:
When listening for keyboard events, you can add key modifiers when using v-on for specific keys like enter, tab, delete, esc, etc.

<input @keyup.enter="submit" />

You can also use system modifier keys like ctrl, alt, shift, and meta to trigger mouse or keyboard event listeners only when the corresponding key is pressed.

steps.text: User interacts with the DOM element (e.g., clicks a button).
Vue captures the native DOM event via the listener.
Any applied event modifiers (like .prevent) are processed.
The bound Vue method or inline expression is executed.
